class.name: NetwPrediction
class.description:
Reached by [member NetwEntity.prediction]. An entity with a [method NetwPropertyConfig.state] property, a [method NetwPropertyConfig.input] property and a [member NetwSimulation.network_process] is predicted. A [RigidBody2D] or [RigidBody3D] needs only the two properties. The client that controls the entity runs that function on its own input each tick, and the server runs it on the same input when it arrives. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"move").input() Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state()
func _network_process(delta: float, tick: int, is_fresh: bool) -> void: velocity = move * SPEED move_and_slide() if is_fresh and is_on_floor(): footstep.play() [/codeblock] A rollback runs this function again for past ticks. Anything it reads besides input and state is not put back, and anything it plays would play twice without the [code]is_fresh[/code] check. [b]When the client is wrong[/b] The client corrects its entity when a state property differs from the server's by more than [member correction_threshold]. Past [member teleport_threshold] the entity jumps straight to the server's state. [member mode] picks the correction. [constant MODE_ROLLBACK] returns to the server's state and runs the newer inputs again. [constant MODE_OFFSET] moves the entity by the difference. [constant MODE_DISABLED] stops predicting and shows the server's state. [b]Rigid bodies[/b] An official Godot build cannot run physics again for a past tick, so a [RigidBody2D] or [RigidBody3D] uses [constant MODE_OFFSET]. The [url=https://github.com/diejor/godot/releases]Networked engine build[/url] can roll one back. It adds [url=https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/76462]physics stepping[/url] and [url=https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/113784]kinematic body updates[/url] to Godot. On another build, install a [NetwPhysicsStepper]. Rigid bodies in the same [NetwInterestLayer] roll back together when the engine can step physics. Turn off [member rollback_together] to correct each one alone. [b]Late and lost input[/b] Raise [member input_buffer_ticks] when a player on a bad connection stutters. The server waits that many ticks before it uses input, so each one adds a tick of delay. [member repeat_missing_input] reuses the last input when one is lost. [b]Debugging[/b] Debug > Networked > Prediction Rings draws rings around each predicted entity. - [b]cyan[/b] where it is drawn - [b]green[/b] where it is simulated - [b]orange[/b] where the server last said it was - [b]dashed magenta[/b] where the client predicted it would be - [b]white line[/b] the gap between orange and magenta

method.name: notify_collision
method.description: Holds off small corrections for [member correction_cooldown_ticks], so a correction does not fight a collision. Call it on the client that controls the entity when its body collides. A rollback is not held off.

members.member: How many ticks [method notify_collision] holds off small corrections. An error past [member teleport_threshold] still teleports.
How many times this peer has corrected the entity.

How far the predicted state may drift from the server's before it is corrected. [method NetwPropertyConfig.correction_threshold] overrides it for one property. An entity with [member NetwSimulation.physics_driven] tolerates one and a half quantizer steps on each quantized property.
How many ticks of input the server keeps queued before it runs them. It then runs one every tick, so an input that arrives late is still in time. Each tick adds a tick of delay.

How far the server may fall behind the newest input before it skips ahead to it. Without this, a client that joins a running session can leave the server behind for good. [code]0[/code] disables skipping.

How many queued inputs the server may run in one tick to catch up to [member input_buffer_ticks] behind the newest input. Each extra input runs [member NetwSimulation.network_process] once more, and none is skipped. It applies to [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_TICK], and an entity at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_FRAME] catches up by running one input per physics frame.
How a misprediction is corrected. Defaults to [constant MODE_AUTO].

If [code]true[/code], this entity stops predicting and follows the server while it touches a moving body this peer does not simulate. It still sends input. It only takes effect on an entity with [member NetwSimulation.physics_driven], whose contacts are read from its bodies.

If [code]true[/code], the server repeats the last input when one is lost. If [code]false[/code], it runs nothing for that input at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_TICK] and runs with zeroed input at the other schedules. Defaults to [code]true[/code] on an entity with [member NetwSimulation.physics_driven].

If [code]true[/code], this entity is corrected together with the predicted entities this peer runs as [constant NetwSimulation.MODE_ACTIVE], rolling them back from the same tick. If [code]false[/code], each entity is corrected on its own. Defaults to [code]true[/code] on an entity with [member NetwSimulation.physics_driven] that runs at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_STEPPED], and [code]false[/code] otherwise.

How large an error may be before a [constant MODE_OFFSET] correction teleports the entity, writing every state property including [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_only] ones. It is measured on properties declared with [method NetwPropertyConfig.extrapolate], and [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_threshold] overrides it for one property. An entity with neither teleports on every such correction. A rollback writes the server's state at any size of error. Defaults to [code]3.0[/code] on an entity with [member NetwSimulation.physics_driven] and [code]2.0[/code] otherwise.

The version of the level this entity moves in, or [code]-1[/code] when unset. Change it when the level changes. For [member correction_cooldown_ticks] after that, a correction writes the server's state outright.

signal.name: corrected
signal.description: Emitted after a correction moved the entity. [param tick] is the tick of the server's state it was corrected against, or the present tick when entities rolled back together. [param teleported] is [code]true[/code] when the correction was a teleport. It is emitted when the [method MultiplayerAPI.poll] or [NetwClock] tick that corrected the entity ends, so a handler reads the entity as that poll or tick left it. [param deltas] holds how far each [float], [Vector2] and [Vector3] state property moved, as [code]after - before[/code], with angles taken the short way around. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┖╴property_name Variant how far that state property moved [/codeblock] Under [constant NetwDisplay.LIVE_MODE_CHASE] the display already smooths the correction away. [codeblock] entity.display.live_mode = NetwDisplay.LIVE_MODE_CHASE entity.display.chase_glide_time = 0.15 [/codeblock]

constants.constant: Return to the server's state and run the newer inputs again. A [RigidBody2D] or [RigidBody3D] at [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_FRAME] cannot run a past tick again, so it uses [constant MODE_OFFSET] and warns once.
Move the entity by the difference between the server's state and what the client predicted, and run nothing again.
Do not predict. The client that controls the entity does not run [member NetwSimulation.network_process] and shows the server's state.
[constant MODE_OFFSET] for a [RigidBody3D] or [RigidBody2D] on any schedule but [constant NetwSimulation.SCHEDULE_STEPPED], and [constant MODE_ROLLBACK] otherwise.
